backups.title: Backups
backups.enable: Back this cluster up to object storage
backups.enableHelp: Turns on WAL archiving and lets you take backups with pgBackRest.
backups.endpointHelp: Full https URL, for example https://s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com. pgBackRest requires TLS.
backups.secretHelp: Name of a Secret in this namespace with keys access-key and secret-key. pglord never stores the keys themselves.
backups.restartNote: Turning backups on or off changes WAL archiving, which needs a cluster restart before it takes effect.
backups.disabled: No backup repository configured for this cluster.
backups.none: No backups yet. Take one to check the repository works.
backups.label: Backup
backups.verifyTlsHelp: Leave on for real object storage. Turn off only if your endpoint uses a self-signed certificate.
backups.scheduleHelp: Standard five-field cron, for example 0 3 * * * for 03:00 daily or 0 3 * * 0 for Sundays. Leave empty to back up only when you ask. Minimum interval is 15 minutes.

kindHelp.full: Everything. Slowest and largest, and the base the others build on.
kindHelp.diff: Only what changed since the last full backup.
kindHelp.incr: Only what changed since the last backup of any type. Smallest and quickest.

workload.title: Placement and resources

antiAffinityHelp.preferred: Instances are spread across nodes when possible, and still schedule if only one node is available.
antiAffinityHelp.required: Instances never share a node. On a cluster with fewer nodes than instances, the extra instances stay pending.
antiAffinityHelp.disabled: Instances may share a node, so one node failure can take the whole cluster down.

workload.resourcesHelp: Quantities like 100m, 1, 256Mi or 2Gi. Leave blank to set no limit.
workload.reservedKey: '{{key}}' is reserved by pglord and cannot be used.

config.title: Configuration
config.pendingRestart: Some settings need a restart before they take effect.
config.restartWarning: Instances restart one at a time, standbys first and the primary last. Connections drop briefly as each instance comes back.

sync.title: Synchronous replication
sync.enableWarning: Every commit will wait until a standby confirms it. If no standby is connected, writes block until one returns. Applies with a reload — no restart.
sync.disableWarning: Commits will no longer wait for a standby. A primary failure can lose the most recent commits.
sync.on: On — commits wait for any one standby ({{count}} connected).
sync.degraded: No synchronous standby is connected — writes are blocked until one returns.

image.title: Change image of {{name}}?
image.label: Image
image.warning: Every instance restarts on the new image, standbys first, the primary last. The image must ship the same PostgreSQL major version — an instance refuses to start otherwise, and reverting the image here rolls the cluster back.

hba.title: Client access rules
hba.explainer: Rules are checked first match wins. pglord always allows replication and local access before your rules and accepts any password-authenticated client after them; add reject rules to tighten access. Changes apply with a reload — no restart.
hba.noneSet: No rules defined — any client with a valid password can connect.

preflight.title: Cluster permissions
preflight.intro: What pglord is allowed to do in its namespace, as reported by the Kubernetes API server.
preflight.allGranted: All required permissions are granted in namespace {{namespace}}.
preflight.missing: {{count}} required permissions are missing in namespace {{namespace}}. Cluster management will fail until they are granted.

secrets.title: Secrets and initialisation
secrets.unsatisfied: Something this cluster depends on is missing. Instances will not start until it exists.

purposes.restore_repository: Object storage this cluster was restored from

secrets.credentialsSecretHelp: Leave empty and pglord generates one. To use your own, create a Secret with keys superuser-password and replication-password first.
secrets.credentialsSecretFixed: The Secret reference is fixed after creation. Use Rotate passwords to change the managed passwords safely; repointing to a different Secret is not supported.
secrets.envHelp: Set on every instance. Init scripts can read them as psql variables, for example :'APP_PASSWORD'.
secrets.initHelp: SQL run once, on the primary, when the data directory is first created. Files ending in .sql run in filename order, so name them 01-…, 02-….
secrets.initSecretHelp: For init SQL containing passwords. Runs after the ConfigMap's scripts. A ConfigMap is readable by anyone with namespace access; a Secret is not.
secrets.initOnceNote: Scripts run only when a cluster is first created. Adding them to an existing cluster has no effect, and a restored cluster never runs them — its data already exists.

errors.name: Use letters, digits and underscores, not starting with a digit.
errors.reserved: {{name}} is set by pglord and cannot be overridden.
errors.incompleteSecret: A secret reference needs both a secret name and a key.

secrets.rotateWarning: New superuser and replication passwords are generated and applied, then every instance restarts one at a time. Connected clients keep working until they reconnect — after that they need the new password from the Secret.

restore.title: Restore into a new cluster
restore.subtitle: Creates a new cluster from {{source}}'s backups. {{source}} itself is not touched.
restore.targetHelp: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes, up to 40 characters. Must differ from the cluster being restored.
restore.fromBackup: The data exactly as backup {{label}} captured it. Nothing written after that backup is included.
restore.fromLatest: The newest backup plus every change archived since — the most recent state the repository can produce.
restore.targetTimeHelp: Replays the write-ahead log up to this moment, then stops. Must be within the range the backups and archived WAL cover.
restore.note: Backups are switched off on the new cluster: it would otherwise write into the repository it was restored from. Configure a repository of its own once you are happy with the data.

clusters.title: Clusters
clusters.name: Name
clusters.nameHelp: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. Max 40 characters.
clusters.storageHelp: Size with unit, for example 1Gi or 500Mi.
clusters.deleteWarning: The cluster and all of its data volumes will be removed. This cannot be undone.
clusters.emptyHint: Create your first HA Postgres cluster to get started.
clusters.hideAdvanced: Hide secrets, environment and init scripts
clusters.imageHelp: Leave empty to use the image this pglord was configured with. Set one only to pin a specific agent image.

clusterDetail.scaleDownWarning: Removing instances deletes their data volumes.
clusterDetail.storageGrowOnly: Storage can only grow, and your StorageClass must allow volume expansion.
clusterDetail.switchoverWarning: The current primary steps down and this instance takes over writes. Connections through the read-write service drop briefly and reconnect.
